### 3. In-conversation output — print the summary in the conversation at the end of the run.

## Stopping condition

The run ends when **any** of:

- The build queue is empty AND (in full mode) the prep queue is empty (`Stop reason: queue-drained` — the normal exit).
- Everything remaining is in a parked / errored state, with no further dispatches possible (`Stop reason: all-remaining-parked`).
- A budget dimension breaches at a between-units check (`faff budget check` returns `breached ≠ []`): `Stop reason = budget-hit(<dims>)` on a `stop` outcome, or `budget-escalated(<dims>)` on an `escalate` outcome (which also emits the structured needs-human signal). `<dims>` names the breached dimension(s) — e.g. `budget-hit(max_attempts)`, `budget-hit(tokens)`. A `narrow` outcome does **not** stop the run — it continues on the methodology's cheapest subset until a `stop` falls through.
- (**by default at L3, at L4 always, or any git-only run — every run except an opted-out L3 tracker run**) `faff run-done` decides the wave-boundary stop (step 8.5): `run-complete` → `Stop reason: converged/both-dry`; `escalate` → `Stop reason: non-convergence` (runaway backstop) / `budget-escalated(<dims>)` / `product-incomplete`, with the structured needs-human signal. A lights-out (L4) run consults it at run-end **regardless of the flag/knob** (convergence is non-optional there) — doneness, not bare queue-emptiness, terminates it; an **opted-out** tracker-mode L3 run (`--no-converge` / `enabled: false`) ends by queue-emptiness and never consults it. A **git-only** plain L3 run has no tracker-observed emptiness to exit on, so it consults `faff run-done` at every wave boundary regardless of level or opt-out (see step 8.5 → _Git-only signal assembly_).
- (**unattended runs — L4, or an L3 that declared `autonomous.unattended` / the `sentry_acting` alias**) a `faff sentry check` returns `abort` on a run that acts: `Stop reason: sentry-abort` — `faff sentry abort` marks the ledger aborted-resumable, no further builds launch, verdicts surfaced. (A `pause` parks the implicated issue(s) and continues — for an unattended run: L4, or an L3 that declared `autonomous.unattended` / the `sentry_acting` alias; an attended L3 logs + surfaces. Not a run-level stop.)

On a budget-hit/escalate, in-flight units complete naturally — see `## Budget flags` for the full mechanics. Issues admitted to the build queue but not yet dispatched are reported under `## Unreached (budget hit)`; they retain Todo + spec state and the next run picks them up. This is the **only** legitimate way to end with a non-empty build queue; the "Never defers a queue" guarantee is otherwise binding (see `## Guarantees`). `Stop reason` is by which condition fires **first**: a set-and-breached budget wins over a would-be `queue-drained` (surface it — the user wants to know if their budget bound or was moot); several dimensions breaching on one check name all of them in `<dims>`; otherwise `queue-drained` / `all-remaining-parked`.

## Autonomous-mode signal to sub-skills

When beep-boop invokes any sub-skill (the `faff-tidy`, `faff-prep`, `faff-graft` skills, each resolved per gateway → **Sibling-skill invocation**), it prefixes the invocation with an explicit autonomous-mode signal:

> _Running in autonomous mode (invoked by /faff-beep-boop, run <run-id>). Skip all prompts. Park on ambiguity. Log everything to `.faff/runs/<run-id>/`. Return structured result to caller._

Sub-skills honour this per their own `Autonomous Mode` sections.

## Guarantees

- **Never prompts the human mid-run for a build/scope/merge/admission decision — this is a hard, harshly-worded invariant, not a soft default.** A mid-run interactive gate is a contract violation. See the gateway's Autonomous Mode Contract → *The no-prompt invariant* + *Banned rationalisations* for the full rule and the enumerated non-reasons — not restated here.
- **Never aborts the run on a single failure.** Park that issue, log, continue with the next unit of work.
- **Never auto-splits tickets** or restructures the backlog beyond what tidy's autonomous defaults allow.
- **Never auto-merges without the three-condition gate** (AC verified + CI green + review returned `pass` — see faff-graft Step 10).
- **Never reports a clean run without confronting the ledger against ground truth** (step 11.5). A `shipped` outcome with no matching merge, or a non-admitted sibling that flipped terminal mid-run, is never silently accepted — L4 lights-out escalates rather than reporting complete; ≤L3 surfaces it in the run summary as a warning. **Nor does it record a prep-return bucket without the same confrontation** (step 3): an attach-expecting return (`refreshed`/`promoted`/`promoted-needs-review`) is never trusted from its own narration — `faff prepcheck --issue` + tracker spec-discovery must confirm the attach before the bucket lands; a mismatch recovers idempotently or re-dispatches once, then records `errored` rather than a phantom success.
- **Never parks work on "scope" or "capacity" grounds.** Every ready-with-spec issue gets attempted. "Too many to do in one session" is explicitly forbidden (see the gateway contract). The run ends when the queue drains or everything remaining is genuinely parked by the three valid categories — not by the orchestrator deciding to do fewer.
- **Never "defers" a queue to the next run.** Identifying a build queue (independents + collision groups, waves mapped) and then ending the run with that queue undispatched is **the same failure as parking it**, regardless of the wording in the summary. Phrases like "12-issue build queue not dispatched this conversation", "queue unblocked, ready for next pass", "deferred to next /faff-beep-boop", "single-conversation context budget" are all banned summaries — they describe a run that bailed on the build pass after doing the analysis.
